claims.claim: An individual pays 25% on the real capital gain accrued from 1.1.2012; the 30% rate applies to a significant shareholder selling a SECURITY (nia'r erech), and a significant shareholder is someone holding 10% or more of any type of means of control. Israel Tax Authority Form 1399y (notice of sale of an asset) sets these rates.
claims.raw_snippet: שיעורי המס - על חלק רווח ההון ריאלי שנצבר החל מיום 1.1.2012 מס בשיעור של עד .25% במכירת נייר ערך בידי בעל מניות מהותי, יחוייב במס בשיעור של .30%

claims.claim: Companies pay the standard corporate tax rate of 23% on capital gains and business income (since 2018).
claims.raw_snippet: Income sourcing rules determine when income is to be considered from an Israeli source. The corporate tax rate is 23% in 2026 (same rate as in 2025). Business operations qualifying under the Encouragement of Capital Investments Law are entitled to reduced rates of tax depending upon their location and other conditions ( see the Tax credits and incentives section ), although a QDMTT shall apply for relevant groups for tax years beginning after 31 December 2025 ( see below ).

claims.claim: If crypto activity is a business, gains are taxed as ordinary income at marginal rates (10% to 47%, with the old shorthand 'up to 50%'), plus National Insurance and health tax.
claims.raw_snippet: Personal income tax rates Taxation of individuals is imposed in graduated rates ranging up to 47%. Additionally, a 3% surtax applies on annual taxable income exceeding ILS 721,560, resulting in a 50% maximum income tax rate. Non-residents are taxed at the same rates as Israeli residents. The annual tax brackets are an aggregation of the monthly brackets in force during the year, which are periodically updated for inflation.
claims.verified_via: cited page fetched and confirmed to contain "47%"; snippet replaced with the page's own wording around it

claims.claim: Surtax (mas yesafim) for 2026: 3% base on all taxable income above NIS 721,560 plus an additional 2% on capital-source income above the same threshold, effective 5% on crypto gains in that band. Threshold NIS 721,560 annual / NIS 60,130 monthly, frozen through tax year 2027 by the December 2024 indexation-pause amendment.
claims.raw_snippet: מס יסף בשנת 2026: 3% על הכנסה החייבת מעל 721,560 ש"ח, ובתוספת 2% על הכנסה הונית מעל אותו סף, כך שעל רווחי הון השיעור הכולל הוא 5%. הסף קפוא לשנים 2025 עד 2027.

claims.claim: Israeli VAT rate is 18% from 1 January 2025 (raised from 17%); applies to business-classified crypto activity such as mining and dealing.
claims.raw_snippet: Israel increased its standard VAT rate to 18% from 17% effective 1 January 2025.

claims.claim: The 2025 Voluntary Disclosure Procedure (hora'at sha'a) applies from publication until 31.08.2026. Requests may be filed only on an identified (non-anonymous) basis, and income-tax cases are handled either by an assessment agreement ('regular track') or by filing corrected/first returns ('green track').
claims.raw_snippet: נוהל זה יחול מיום פרסומו ועד ליום 31.08.2026 בכל מקרה של אי התאמה או מחלוקת - האמור בנוהל גילוי מרצון קובע.

claims.claim: Israel is among the jurisdictions committed to the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF); Israeli RCASPs collect customer data from 2026, with first international exchange expected 2027-2028. The exact first-exchange year has shifted between OECD monitoring updates and must be verified against the latest OECD commitments list.

claims.claim: Self-employed National Insurance 2026: 4.47% on monthly income up to about NIS 7,703, 12.83% on the portion above. Health tax 3.23% / 5.17% across the same bands. Combined roughly 7.7% / 18%. Applies only to business-classified income.
claims.raw_snippet: דמי ביטוח לאומי לעצמאי 2026: 4.47% עד 7,703 ש"ח לחודש, 12.83% מעל; דמי ביטוח בריאות 3.23% / 5.17%.

claims.claim: Form 909 lets an individual taxpayer who realised a gain from virtual currency pay the tax due on that realisation when the Israeli commercial banking system refused to accept them, including refusal to open an account. The procedure is a temporary Israel Tax Authority order issued together with the Bank of Israel and the Anti-Money-Laundering Authority; companies cannot use the service. The assessing officer sets the tax liability in an assessment agreement under Section 145(a)(2)(b) or Section 145a2(a1) of the Ordinance.
claims.raw_snippet: שירות זה מאפשר לנישומים יחידים שצברו רווח ממימוש מטבעות וירטואליים, לשלם את המס המגיע מהמימוש בתנאי שהמערכת הבנקאית המסחרית בישראל סירבה לקבלם, כולל סירוב לפתוח חשבון.

claims.claim: A TY2025 draft amendment to the exemption-from-filing regulations exempts a salaried taxpayer from the annual return on crypto gains when traded through a supervised Israeli platform that withheld tax at source and total income stays under the Section 131 ceilings (about NIS 723,000 gross from work/business, or NIS 721,560 total taxable income). Exceeding the ceiling restores the Section 131 filing duty. Still in draft as of mid-2026.
claims.raw_snippet: טיוטת תקנות מס הכנסה (פטור מהגשת דין וחשבון) 2025: שכיר יהיה פטור מהגשת דוח על רווחי קריפטו אם המסחר בוצע דרך גוף מפוקח בישראל שניכה מס במקור, וכל עוד ההכנסה אינה עולה על תקרת סעיף 131 (כ-723,000 ש"ח מעבודה/עסק או 721,560 ש"ח הכנסה חייבת כוללת).

claims.claim: Section 131 of the Income Tax Ordinance defines who must file an annual return; a person is not required to file while annual income does not exceed the amount set in Schedule B to the Income Tax Regulations (Exemption from Filing a Return), 1988.

claims.claim: Capital losses carried forward from previous years (subject to limits) may be offset against capital gains: 1:1 against the real gain, and at a ratio of 3.5 NIS of chargeable inflationary amount per 1 NIS of capital loss. The skill body cites Section 92 / סעיף 92 of the Income Tax Ordinance as the loss-offset provision; the Form 1399y instruction quoted here evidences the offsetting rule and its ratios, not the section number itself.

claims.claim: A capital gain is split into a real-gain component and an inflationary amount; the real gain accrued from 1.1.2012 is taxed at up to 25%. The calculator does not apply this split.
claims.raw_snippet: שיעורי המס - על חלק רווח ההון ריאלי שנצבר החל מיום 1.1.2012 מס בשיעור של עד .25% במכירת נייר ערך בידי בעל מניות מהותי, יחוייב במס בשיעור של .30%

claims.claim: A new immigrant (oleh chadash) or veteran returning resident (toshav chozer vatik) is entitled under Section 14(a) of the Income Tax Ordinance to a 10-year exemption, from the date of becoming an Israeli resident, on income and capital gains sourced from assets held abroad; this can reach crypto acquired abroad before aliyah.
claims.raw_snippet: לפי סעיף 14(א) לפקודת מס הכנסה, עולה חדש ותושב חוזר ותיק זכאים לפטור ממס למשך 10 שנים על הכנסות שהופקו מחוץ לישראל, כולל רווחי הון ממכירת נכסים בחו"ל.

claims.claim: ITA Circular 05/2018 (17 January 2018) is the primary crypto-tax guidance: the sale of a decentralised means of payment is taxed as the sale of an 'asset' under Chapter E of the Income Tax Ordinance, classified as capital income, at the rates set in Section 91. Income reaching the level of a business is fruit income (Section 2 sources) taxed under Sections 121 or 126, not as a capital gain.
claims.raw_snippet: מכירת אמצעי תשלום מבוזר תמוסה כמכירת "נכס" בהתאם לחלק ה' לפקודת מס הכנסה -, תסווג כהכנסה הונית ותחויב במס רווח הון בהתאם לשיעורי המס הקבועים בסעיף 91 לפקודה.

claims.claim: Crypto service providers in Israel operate under the Prohibition on Money Laundering Order; a NIS 50,000 per-six-months ceiling applies to casual-customer activity before full identification/recording duties attach. This provider AML reporting is separate from the taxpayer's tax-reporting duty.
claims.raw_snippet: צו איסור הלבנת הון לנותני שירות בנכס פיננסי: סף לקוח מזדמן של 50,000 ש"ח לתקופה של שישה חודשים.

claims.claim: Bank of Israel publishes daily representative rates (sha'ar yatzig) used to convert foreign-fiat legs of crypto trades to NIS.
claims.raw_snippet: בנק ישראל מפרסם שערים יציגים יומיים.

claims.claim: A person reporting the sale of a decentralised means of payment must retain documents proving that the reported income came from such a sale, to the satisfaction of the assessing officer.
claims.raw_snippet: אדם המדווח על מכירת אמצעי תשלום מבוזר ישמור מסמכים להוכחה כי ההכנסות המדווחות הן ממכירת אמצעי תשלום מבוזר המשמש לצורך סחר חליפין ככול שיידרש להנחת דעתו של פקיד השומה.

claims.claim: Section 100A (סעיף 100א) of the Income Tax Ordinance imposes an exit tax: a person ceasing Israeli residency is deemed to have sold all their assets (crypto included) one day before residency ends. The tax may be paid at exit or deferred to the actual later sale, with the gain apportioned over the Israeli-residency period. Separately, business-classified miners and NFT creators may deduct direct costs (electricity, depreciation) under Section 17 of the Ordinance.
claims.raw_snippet: Israel imposes an exit tax under Section 100A (סעיף 100א): an individual who ceases to be an Israeli resident is deemed to have sold their assets one day before ceasing residency; tax can be deferred until actual realisation with apportionment of the gain. Business expenses are deductible under Section 17.

claims.claim: The definition of 'asset' in Section 88 of the Income Tax Ordinance covers all property, tangible or intangible; a decentralised means of payment is the property of the person holding it and is therefore included in that definition.
claims.raw_snippet: הגדרת "נכס" בסעיף 88 לפקודת מס הכנסה כוללת בין היתר כל רכוש, בין אם מדובר בנכס מוחשי ובין אם מדובר בנכס לא מוחשי. אמצעי תשלום מבוזר מהווה רכושו של האדם המחזיק בו, ומשכך הוא נכלל בהגדרת "נכס" בסעיף 88 לפקודה.

claims.claim: Green-track criterion for digital assets in Income Tax Execution Instruction 10/2025: the disclosed income from digital assets does not exceed 500,000 NIS for the WHOLE disclosure period (not per year), and the fair value of all digital assets as at 31/12/2024 does not exceed 1,500,000 NIS. Expressed in the skill body as up to 1.5 million NIS / 1.5 ₪ million of digital assets.
